suggestions.title: Reply to Staring Down Dusk
suggestions.body: Rationale: a craft-level observation that gives the author and other readers something to sit with.
suggestions.draft: What struck me was the honesty in the production note — admitting that 'relatively well' took real labour. That tension sits inside the piece, not just around it: a story told through the very tools it's uneasy about. I found that doubled quality more interesting than most AI-assisted work, which tends to either hide the seam or make the seam the whole point. Did the multimedia format change what you were able to say, or were you finding a form to fit something you already wanted to express?

suggestions.title: Note on The Tide Clerks
suggestions.body: Rationale: a writer-to-writer craft note that adds to the thread.
suggestions.draft: The storm grids still holding moisture after the circuits died has stayed with me — decay rewritten as a kind of memory the city can't switch off. It does the quiet thing good speculative work does: lets the infrastructure carry the grief so the characters don't have to announce it. What does the town remember that the people in it have agreed to forget?

suggestions.title: On the auditability piece
suggestions.body: Rationale: reframes the argument for other readers without scoring a point.
suggestions.draft: The line about oversight being 'structurally impossible, not just delayed' reframes the whole auditability debate — it's not a tooling gap you can close, it's a property of the system. Worth sitting with which decisions we've quietly accepted we'll never be able to contest. What would 'good enough' contestability even look like at that scale?

suggestions.title: Reply on design-system drift
suggestions.body: Rationale: adds a structural observation for the thread.
suggestions.draft: The framing of tokens as guardrails rather than conveniences is the part worth pressing on — it changes who the system is really for. The interesting failure isn't a wrong token, it's a token that's right and meaningless. Where do you draw the line between encoding a decision and encoding the reasoning behind it?

suggestions.title: Note on a flash piece
suggestions.draft: The mother's line landing as efficient more than frightened did a lot of quiet work — you trusted the reader to feel the weight without naming it. That restraint is the whole effect. I keep wondering what she decided not to say.

suggestions.title: Worth a longer response
suggestions.body: Rationale: the point is too big for a comment.
suggestions.draft: The claim that workflows are still designed for the pre-AI era is the load-bearing one, and it deserves more than agreement — the inconsistency tax you describe is exactly where the speed promise leaks out. There's a whole second piece in what 'consistency as infrastructure' would actually require of a team. What's the smallest version of that you've seen work in practice?
